Together with their endpoints — 35 rigid sets: the 34 three-distance sets and the regular pentagon — they form a graph with 108 arcs between rigid sets (connected, first Betti number 74), 77 arcs ending in a degenerate configuration and 12 escaping to infinity; every rigid set with fewer distances is the limit of some family. 6,4.title: The 149 6-point 4-distance sets and 4 families
6,4.note: Rigid configurations first, then one representative of each family (a family = a realizable pattern of equal pairs; its dimension is measured in the full configuration space).
sources: F. Szöllősi, P. R. J. Östergård, Constructions of maximum few-distance sets in Euclidean spaces, Electron. J. Combin. 27(1) (2020) P1.23

exact classification for this applet (Oct 2026): complete list of candidate distance patterns (a re-implementation of the Szöllősi–Östergård orderly generation, reproducing their counts at every order), every pattern certified rigid (Singular, dimension 0 over ℚ) and solved by msolve real root isolation; configurations counted up to similarity by an exact congruence test. Code, certificates and write-ups: https://github.com/alonamit1729/affinemess-applets/tree/main/tools/fixed-distances (walkthrough: https://github.com/alonamit1729/affinemess-applets/blob/main/tools/fixed-distances/g7count/REPRODUCING.md)

7,5.title: The 508 7-point 5-distance sets and 9 families
7,5.note: Rigid configurations first, then one representative of each family (a family = a realizable pattern of equal pairs; its dimension is measured in the full configuration space).
sources: F. Szöllősi, P. R. J. Östergård, Constructions of maximum few-distance sets in Euclidean spaces, Electron. J. Combin. 27(1) (2020) P1.23

exact classification for this applet (Oct 2026): complete list of candidate distance patterns (a re-implementation of the Szöllősi–Östergård orderly generation, reproducing their counts at every order), every pattern certified rigid (Singular, dimension 0 over ℚ) and solved by msolve real root isolation; configurations counted up to similarity by an exact congruence test. Code, certificates and write-ups: https://github.com/alonamit1729/affinemess-applets/tree/main/tools/fixed-distances (walkthrough: https://github.com/alonamit1729/affinemess-applets/blob/main/tools/fixed-distances/g7count/REPRODUCING.md)

8,5.title: The 165 8-point 5-distance sets and 2 families
8,5.note: Rigid configurations first, then one representative of each family (a family = a realizable pattern of equal pairs; its dimension is measured in the full configuration space).
sources: F. Szöllősi, P. R. J. Östergård, Constructions of maximum few-distance sets in Euclidean spaces, Electron. J. Combin. 27(1) (2020) P1.23

exact classification for this applet (Oct 2026): complete list of candidate distance patterns (a re-implementation of the Szöllősi–Östergård orderly generation, reproducing their counts at every order), every pattern certified rigid (Singular, dimension 0 over ℚ) and solved by msolve real root isolation; configurations counted up to similarity by an exact congruence test. Code, certificates and write-ups: https://github.com/alonamit1729/affinemess-applets/tree/main/tools/fixed-distances (walkthrough: https://github.com/alonamit1729/affinemess-applets/blob/main/tools/fixed-distances/g7count/REPRODUCING.md)

9,6.title: The 698 9-point 6-distance sets and the family
9,6.note: Rigid configurations first, then one representative of each family (a family = a realizable pattern of equal pairs; its dimension is measured in the full configuration space).
sources: F. Szöllősi, P. R. J. Östergård, Constructions of maximum few-distance sets in Euclidean spaces, Electron. J. Combin. 27(1) (2020) P1.23

exact classification for this applet (Oct 2026): complete list of candidate distance patterns (a re-implementation of the Szöllősi–Östergård orderly generation, reproducing their counts at every order), every pattern certified rigid (Singular, dimension 0 over ℚ) and solved by msolve real root isolation; configurations counted up to similarity by an exact congruence test. Code, certificates and write-ups: https://github.com/alonamit1729/affinemess-applets/tree/main/tools/fixed-distances (walkthrough: https://github.com/alonamit1729/affinemess-applets/blob/main/tools/fixed-distances/g7count/REPRODUCING.md)

sources: F. Szöllősi, P. R. J. Östergård, Constructions of maximum few-distance sets in Euclidean spaces, Electron. J. Combin. 27(1) (2020) P1.23

exact classification for this applet (Oct 2026): complete list of candidate distance patterns (a re-implementation of the Szöllősi–Östergård orderly generation, reproducing their counts at every order), every pattern certified rigid (Singular, dimension 0 over ℚ) and solved by msolve real root isolation; configurations counted up to similarity by an exact congruence test. sources: F. Szöllősi, P. R. J. Östergård, Constructions of maximum few-distance sets in Euclidean spaces, Electron. J. Combin. 27(1) (2020) P1.23
A. Amit, GPT-6 Astra, The maximum cardinality of a planar seven-distance set, preprint (24 October 2026), submitted to Hexagon

exact classification for this applet (Oct 2026): complete list of candidate distance patterns (a re-implementation of the Szöllősi–Östergård orderly generation, reproducing their counts at every order), every pattern certified rigid (Singular, dimension 0 over ℚ) and solved by msolve real root isolation; configurations counted up to similarity by an exact congruence test.
